issues.failure_explanation: With U_j and lambda_j exactly as defined, C_alpha(Gamma_alpha^{-1}U_j) = conj(lambda_j)(Gamma_alpha^{-1}U_j): since C_1 U_j = omega_j^{-1} U_j and C_alpha = alpha^{1/ell} Gamma^{-1} C_1 Gamma, the Fourier mode U_j pairs with the conjugate eigenvalue. Hence C_alpha = Gamma_alpha^{-1} U barLambda U^* Gamma_alpha, not Gamma_alpha^{-1} U Lambda U^* Gamma_alpha; concretely, for ell >= 3 the matrix Gamma^{-1}U Lambda U^* Gamma has its nonzero entries on the superdiagonal, whereas C_alpha has 1's on the subdiagonal and alpha in the top-right corner. The paper assumes even ell > 2 (so ell >= 4), for which the two matrices differ; therefore the second line of the align eq:palpha, the displayed factorization, and eq:Paform are false as written (they become true only after conjugating U, or replacing Lambda by barLambda).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Conjugate the Fourier matrix (replace U by its conjugate, i.e. flip the exponent signs in the definition of U_j, or equivalently replace Lambda by barLambda) so that C_alpha = Gamma_alpha^{-1} U Lambda U^* Gamma_alpha holds; eq:palpha and eq:Paform then hold verbatim and all downstream content is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The stated Kronecker factorizations of P_alpha and P_alpha^{-1} are incorrect as identities; an implementation following eq:Paform literally with the stated U and Lambda would apply a mirrored alpha-circulant operator instead of P_alpha^{-1}. Because conjugation only permutes the scaled roots of unity, the set of inner sub-problems (A - lambda_j I)x_j = b_j, the spectral results of Section 2.1, and the numerical methods are unaffected once the convention is fixed.
issues.title: Wrong conjugation in the Fourier diagonalization of C_alpha; eq:palpha and eq:Paform are false as written
issues.why_classification: A one-line convention correction repairs both displays; every substantive claim, algorithm, guarantee and numerical result survives unchanged, so the repair is short, local and routine with no mathematical loss.

It is well known \cite[Sec 5.3 and Appendix B]{axelsson1996iterative} that when $S_j$ consists solely of positive real eigenvalues, CI selects $\poly_p$ as the shifted-and-scaled Chebyshev polynomials. These solve the minimax problem
Note that, for $j' \in \{1, \ell/2 + 1\}$, $\Im(\lambda_j') = 0$. Hence, $B_{j'}$ has real eigenvalues.

issues.failure_explanation: The proposition is stated for B_j = A - lambda_j I with no restriction on lambda_j, so it includes the real roots j' in {1, ell/2+1}. For these, xi_{j'}^{(1)} and xi_{j'}^{(N)} are positive real numbers, hence positively collinear, so |xi^{(1)}+xi^{(N)}| = |xi^{(1)}|+|xi^{(N)}| and the optimal degree-1 polynomial coincides with the scaled Chebyshev polynomial (as the paper itself asserts for real spectra): the claimed strict inequality is an equality, and the proof's inference 'As Re(xi^{(1)}) != Re(xi^{(N)}) it is straightforward to show [strict <]' is invalid in this case. Strictness requires Im(lambda_j) != 0 (non-collinear endpoints).

failure_location.quote: For $p=1$ the maximal value of the optimal polynomial $\poly^*_1$ is strictly smaller than the maximum value of the scaled Chebyshev polynomial

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis Im(lambda_j) != 0 (i.e. restrict the statement to complex scaled roots of unity, as the surrounding discussion intends); the proof then goes through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: As stated the proposition is false for the two real shifts; the intended conclusion (Chebyshev non-optimality for complex scaled roots of unity) is unaffected, and no labelled result relies on the proposition.
issues.title: prop:added-1 claims strict Chebyshev non-optimality without excluding the real shifts
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard local hypothesis that the context already assumes repairs the statement; the method, conclusion and intended scope are unchanged and nothing depends on the defective version.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The corresponding saddle point problem for \eqref{eq:blockproblem} is then given by

issues.failure_explanation: Writing x_j = x^R + i x^I, b_j = b^R + i b^I and Psi = A - Re(lambda_j)I, the complex system is equivalent to Psi x^R + Im(lambda_j) x^I = b^R and Psi x^I - Im(lambda_j) x^R = b^I. Multiplying the displayed matrix S by (Re(x_j), -Im(x_j))^T gives (Im(lambda_j)x^R - Psi x^I, Psi x^R + Im(lambda_j)x^I)^T = (-Im(b_j), Re(b_j))^T, not (-Re(b_j), Im(b_j))^T. Scalar counterexample: A = [2], lambda_j = 0.5 + i, b_j = 1 + 2i gives x_j = -0.1538 + 1.2308i and S(Re x_j, -Im x_j)^T = (-2, 1)^T, whereas the displayed right-hand side is (-1, 2)^T. The displayed system therefore does not solve eq:blockproblem, contrary to the claimed correspondence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side of eq:saddlesystem by (-Im(b_j), Re(b_j))^T, keeping the matrix and the unknown vector (Re(x_j), -Im(x_j))^T as displayed.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted equivalence between the saddle-point system and the complex sub-problem is false as written; a literal implementation of the P_SP inner solve would compute the wrong vector. The eigenvalue analysis of Theorem thm:added-2 uses only the matrix S and is unaffected, and the reported numerics evidently correspond to a correct implementation.
issues.title: Saddle-point reformulation eq:saddlesystem has the wrong right-hand side
issues.why_classification: Given the displayed matrix and unknown, the correct right-hand side is uniquely determined, so the repair is a forced local correction with no effect on any theorem, algorithm guarantee or numerical claim.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For complex roots $\lambda_j$, $j \in [2,\ell/2]\cup [\ell/2+2,\ell]$, we solve \eqref{eq:saddlesystem} using MINRES
The remaining $\lambda_j$ have non-zero complex part with $\lambda_j = \overline{\lambda}_{\ell+2-j}$
This has the form of $S_2^{-1}S$ in \cite[Theorem 4]{pearson2012new}, with $\psimat = \frac{1}{\beta}M$, $\phimat = \frac{1}{\sqrt{\beta}}K$

issues.failure_explanation: In the reformulation Phi = Im(lambda_j) I_N, which is negative definite for every root with Im(lambda_j) < 0, i.e. j in [ell/2+2, ell] — half of the complex sub-problems that Section 5.3 explicitly assigns to this method. For these j the claim that Phi and Psi are symmetric positive definite is false, and the proof invokes [pearson2012new, Theorem 4] outside its hypotheses. Directly, from the proof's own relation zeta^2 = v^T(Psi + Phi Psi^{-1} Phi)v / v^T(Phi+Psi) Psi^{-1} (Phi+Psi)v with v^T Phi v < 0 one gets zeta^2 > 1, so all eigenvalues of P_D^{-1}S lie strictly outside the claimed interval; moreover Phi + Psi = A + (Im(lambda_j)-Re(lambda_j))I, and in the paper's own experiments (alpha = 1, mu_min approximately 1.05, e.g. lambda_9 = 0.309-0.951i and lambda_10 = 0.809-0.588i with Re(lambda_j) - Im(lambda_j) approximately 1.26-1.40 > mu_min) Phi + Psi, and hence the MINRES preconditioner P_D, is indefinite.

failure_location.quote: The eigenvalues of the preconditioned system $\mathcal{P}_{D}^{-1}\mathcal{S}$ lie in  $\big[-1,-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\big] \cup \big[\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},1\big]$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict Theorem thm:added-2 and the SPD claim to Im(lambda_j) > 0, and handle Im(lambda_j) < 0 by solving the conjugate system (A - conj(lambda_j) I) conj(x_j) = conj(b_j) (equivalently, use Phi = |Im(lambda_j)| I with correspondingly adjusted signs); all bounds and the method's behaviour are then recovered.
issues.overall_effect: The eigenvalue inclusion of Theorem thm:added-2 and the SPD property of P_D fail for all complex sub-problems with negative imaginary part, which the P_SP method includes by construction; for those sub-problems MINRES with P_D has no stated guarantee (P_D is not SPD, and in the alpha = 1 regime studied it is indefinite), so the inner-convergence guarantee for P_SP is unsupported for half of its sub-problems.
issues.title: thm:added-2 fails for roots with negative imaginary part: Phi = Im(lambda_j) I is not positive definite
issues.why_classification: The stated theorem is false for a non-degenerate, explicitly used range (half the complex roots, including the paper's alpha = 1 experiments), and the repair needs a hypothesis plus a conjugation step in the construction; the fix is contained and preserves every substantive claim, rate and scope, so it is more than minor but not serious.

With kappa(Re(B_j)) = (mu_max - Re lambda_j)/(mu_min - Re lambda_j) and the appendix values mu_min approximately 1.049 and mu_max approximately 205, Algorithm 1 gives normalized weights r_1 approximately 0.304 (for lambda_1 = 1) and r_6 approximately 0.047 (for lambda_6 = -1), i.e. allocations floor(0.304*200) = 60 and floor(0.047*200) = 9, not 30 and 4; the quoted (30, 4) are the eta = 0.1 allocations (floor(0.304*100) = 30, floor(0.047*100) = 4). The paper's own tables corroborate the eta = 0.2 values: for P_NC2 at n_x = 100, eta = 0.2, alpha = 1 the entry 16 (3248) satisfies 3248 = 16*(10 + 193), where 193 = 60+27+15+11+9+9+9+11+15+27 is the sum of floored allocations at budget 200 (similarly 3710 = 70*(10+43) at n_x = 50, eta = 0.1), whereas allocations starting (30, 4, ...) would sum to about 99. The quoted equal tolerance '(0.6 for alpha = 1)' likewise matches (30, 4), which gives roughly 0.68-0.75, rather than the actual (60, 9), which gives roughly 0.3.
